title: Moby-Dick, Ch. 2 — The Carpet-Bag: Action Spine and Frames
adaptation_principle: Condense the chapter to Ishmael’s concrete movement: arrival, delay, frugal lodging hunt, misstep into a church, and resolve for the Spouter Inn; fold digressions and comparisons into captions or omit them when they don’t change the action.
action_oriented_synopsis: I arrive in New Bedford with my carpet-bag and discover the Nantucket packet has sailed, forcing me to wait until Monday. With little silver, I decide to find cheap lodging for the intervening nights and to ask prices without being particular. I pass the jolly, costly inns and head waterward, limping on patched boots toward the cheapest quarters. I blunder into a negro church, choke on ash, take in the fierce sermon, and back out again. I come upon the Spouter Inn, weigh its ominous sign against my purse, judge it cheap, and resolve to try it.

caption_spine: Quitting old Manhatto with my carpet-bag, I came to New Bedford, only to learn the Nantucket packet had sailed, and I must wait till Monday.
With but a few pieces of silver, I set about finding where to eat and sleep, resolving to inquire the price and not be too particular.
I passed the Crossed Harpoons and the Sword-Fish—too expensive and jolly—and by instinct followed the streets waterward for the cheapest inns, my patched boots weary on the flinty frost.
Blundering through an open door, I stumbled over an ash-box into a negro church, a black Angel of Doom beating a book, and, muttering wretched entertainment at the sign of the Trap, I backed out.

I came upon the Spouter Inn with its creaking sign and the name Peter Coffin—ominous enough—yet I judged it the very spot for cheap lodgings, scraped the ice from my feet, and resolved to see what sort of a place it might be.

Coffin?—Spouter?—Rather ominous in that particular connexion, thought I.
I thought that here was the very spot for cheap lodgings, and the best of pea coffee.
